strings.name: Mike Tyson
strings.summary: Trained in Cus D'Amato's system, Tyson combined rapid pressure with powerful combinations. He won a heavyweight world title at twenty and unified three major belts. His sporting and commercial prominence also encompasses a rape conviction, imprisonment and disqualification for biting an opponent. He later worked in entertainment and business, lost to Jake Paul in 2024, and had an announced 2026 exhibition postponed following injury.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: An iconic heavyweight champion with substantial influence on professional boxing's business and popular culture.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Brooklyn, New York, and raised in Brownsville.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Youngest heavyweight champion
strings.highlights.h1.text: Defeated Trevor Berbick for the WBC title at twenty in 1986.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Introduced to boxing by Bobby Stewart and subsequently trained by Cus D'Amato.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Unified heavyweight titles
strings.highlights.h2.text: Held the WBC, WBA and IBF belts together in 1987.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Exhibition postponement
strings.timeline.t1.text: Promoters cited a broken hand for delaying the Mayweather exhibition; this does not establish a completed fight.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Loses to Jake Paul
strings.timeline.t2.text: Lost a professional bout in Texas by unanimous decision.
strings.timeline.t3.title: International Boxing Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received induction recognizing his professional career.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Disqualified for biting
strings.timeline.t4.text: Disqualified for biting Evander Holyfield's ears during their rematch.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Rape conviction and imprisonment
strings.timeline.t5.text: Convicted of rape and sentenced to six years; released after about three years.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Upset championship defeat
strings.timeline.t6.text: Lost the undisputed title to James Douglas in Tokyo.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completes title unification
strings.timeline.t7.text: Beat Tony Tucker to add the IBF belt to his WBC and WBA titles.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First world championship
strings.timeline.t8.text: Stopped Berbick in round two to become the youngest heavyweight champion.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Turns professional
strings.timeline.t9.text: Began a professional career that drew attention through consecutive knockouts.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Training with D'Amato
strings.timeline.t10.text: Stewart introduced him to systematic training in Catskill.
